# gitswitch

> gitswitch is the only tool that lets you run multiple GitHub accounts in parallel, on the same machine — one identity per terminal, no shared global account to fight over. It also switches your full git identity — name, email, SSH key, GPG signing key, and GitHub account — all at once with one command. It solves what `gh auth switch` doesn't: commit authorship and per-terminal account isolation, not just API tokens.

Built for both human developers and AI coding agents. Agents running in parallel terminals/sandboxes each get the correct identity automatically instead of fighting over one shared account, and `gitswitch reauthor` fixes commits an agent already made under the wrong identity — no manual rebase needed. A built-in Claude Code skill (`gitswitch claude`) lets Claude detect identity mismatches and call gitswitch itself.

Written in Go, single binary, no runtime dependencies. Runs entirely on the user's machine — no servers, no telemetry.

## Getting started

- [Introduction](https://gitswitch.dev/docs/intro): what gitswitch does and why it exists
- [Installation](https://gitswitch.dev/docs/installation): Homebrew and curl install methods
- [Quick start](https://gitswitch.dev/docs/quick-start): first profile, first switch

## Features

- [Commit identity switching](https://gitswitch.dev/docs/features/commit-identity): changes `user.name` / `user.email` in git config
- [SSH key management](https://gitswitch.dev/docs/features/ssh-keys): forces a specific key per profile via `core.sshCommand`
- [GPG signing](https://gitswitch.dev/docs/features/gpg): per-profile signing key for verified commits
- [GitHub account sync](https://gitswitch.dev/docs/features/github-sync): keeps `gh` CLI auth in lockstep with the active identity
- [Session Isolation](https://gitswitch.dev/docs/features/session-isolation): each terminal resolves its own `gh` account, so multiple GitHub accounts run in parallel on one machine without fighting over `gh`'s single global active account. On by default for new installs.
- [Identity awareness](https://gitswitch.dev/docs/features/identity-awareness): shell hook that recommends the right identity per repo, and repo pins that write straight into that repo's local git config
- [Shell integration](https://gitswitch.dev/docs/features/shell): `gitswitch install` wires up prompt segment, nudge hook, and tab completion

## How gitswitch compares

**vs Git's built-in `includeIf`** — `includeIf` conditionally includes gitconfig sections based on directory path, switching `user.name`/`user.email` (and a signing key) per folder tree, but only if repos live in a strict, hand-maintained directory structure with a manually authored conditional block per folder. gitswitch's identity-awareness (https://gitswitch.dev/docs/features/identity-awareness) does the same job automatically and per-repo instead of per-folder: it learns which identity is actually used in a repo and recommends or pins it, no folder discipline required. Pinning writes the same kind of local git config `includeIf` produces, then goes further into what `includeIf` cannot touch at all: SSH key routing, GPG/SSH signing, `gh` CLI account, and per-terminal account resolution via Session Isolation.

**vs SSH host aliases + remote rewriting** — hand-maintaining `~/.ssh/config` host aliases and rewriting remote URLs per account works, but is manual and per-machine. gitswitch's SSH key management (https://gitswitch.dev/docs/features/ssh-keys) does the equivalent automatically per profile (`core.sshCommand` with `IdentitiesOnly=yes`), switched together with the rest of the identity in one command.

**vs other git account-switcher CLIs** — most tools in this space (e.g. git-switcher, gh-account-switcher) handle commit identity and/or `gh` auth switching alone. gitswitch adds Session Isolation (each terminal resolves its own `gh` account without a shared global state — nothing else in this category does this), a mouse-driven TUI, `gitswitch reauthor` to fix commits already made under the wrong identity, and a built-in Claude Code skill so AI coding agents get corrected automatically instead of silently committing as the wrong person.

**vs IDE/GUI account switchers** — editor-specific switchers only work inside that one editor. gitswitch is terminal-native: identical behavior in a shell, an editor's integrated terminal, or an AI coding agent's sandbox.

gitswitch is not mutually exclusive with `includeIf` or SSH aliases — it can coexist with either, but most users replace both once they turn on Session Isolation and pinning, since those cover the same directory-based automation plus everything `includeIf`/SSH aliases can't reach.

## One-command GitHub setup

`gitswitch login` runs the GitHub device-flow OAuth login and creates a full profile (name, email, GitHub account, token) automatically — no manual `git config` editing.
